subject: Relational operators
notes: Rule: '< is an abbreviation for LESS THAN.' (cite.py --check 8.7.5.2 -> OK §8.7.5.2 5)). The grammar admits '<' (comparisonOperator alt) and MapOperator normalizes the concatenated token text (IS/THAN/TO stripped, NOT inverts) so '<' and 'LESS THAN' map to the same C# operator; the >>IF evaluator's private copy is textually identical. Probe probe/relop/relpos.cob (A=5 vs B=3 and B=5, IF with every printed spelling, --std 2023 and 85): the symbol and word forms give identical truth values at both data points (AB TTTFFFFFF|TTTTTFFFFFTTT / AC FFFFFFTTT|TTTTTTTTTTFFF at both editions), all as derived from the rule.
